# Amaterasu — the app, running, on your machine

**Nature: Transmuter.** It executes declared machinery and starts a long-running local process; it
writes no code and sends nothing anywhere, a **deploy** living behind **G3**.

> **Build the thing I am working on and start it on the target I said, from the directory I actually
> work in, and tell me the exact command so I can run it myself.**

Phase four of `ren`, after [`kokusen`](../kokusen/SKILL.md) and before the turn's report; it never
pushes and never opens anything. **The declaration it executes is
[`docs/LAUNCH-MIGRATION.md`](../../../docs/LAUNCH-MIGRATION.md) § *Launch declaration rules*** — the
block's keys, `readyWhen`, the probe's three outcomes, the byte-for-byte name match, the verb-builds /
after-steps-install-and-launch split and how `{artifact}` resolves.

## 0. Standalone entry

[`docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md`](../../../docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md) is the contract, and amaterasu is
already the most cold-ready phase: cold it adds **P1** ([`hatsu-warmup`](../hatsu-warmup/SKILL.md))
and **P2**, read with § 3 — the branch, clean-or-dirty, and **whether this is a worktree**, a session
standing in one **reporting the command rather than running it**. From any composite, skip it; shared
policy is resolved at the plugin root as `hatsu-warmup` § 0 says. **The launch shows the tree on disk,
not a commit**, so name it with the uncommitted paths, and nobody reads a running app as a
demonstration of a recorded change.

## 1. Invocation

```
/amaterasu [<target>]        # <target> names a key of nen/contract.json → project.launch
```

With no argument the target is `nen/workflow.json` → `launch.default`. **There is no built-in default
and none is ever guessed**: launching the wrong build onto the wrong device is not undone by launching
it again.

| What the declaration says | What amaterasu does |
|---|---|
| `project.launch` **absent** or **empty** | record `no launch target declared; skipped`, naming `nen/contract.json`, and continue |
| `launch.default` **`null`**, no argument, **no** declared targets | the same, naming `launch.default` |
| `launch.default` **`null`** but targets **are** declared, no argument | **the case that asks**: list what is declared and ask which |
| an argument naming an undeclared target | refuse by name, list what is declared, continue — **never a near-match** |

**Asking on the no-launch case is the defect**: `ren` is automatic, so a question a repository's
configuration already answered costs one per turn and trains the maintainer to dismiss the phase. No
question, no stop, no bell — continue to [`rikugan`](../rikugan/SKILL.md) and
[`jutaisho`](../jutaisho/SKILL.md).

## 2. The parameters, and the completion the launch owes

| Value | File → key |
|---|---|
| The default target and the disconnected-device fallback | `nen/workflow.json` → `launch.default`, `launch.fallback` |
| The targets — verb, args, device, after-steps, lane, artifact | `nen/contract.json` → `project.launch.<target>` (LAUNCH-MIGRATION) |
| The verb's command line, and where it runs | `project.verbs.<lane>.<verb>`, `project.lanes.<lane>.cwd` |

**`nen shu dev|run --target <name>` executes the whole block** — the probe, the lane's verb with
`args` appended, then the after-steps with both substitutions. **With no `nen/workflow.json`**, say
*"no workflow.json: using the built-in defaults from `docs/WORKFLOW.md`"* and note the cost: they
carry **no** `launch.default` and **no** `launch.fallback`, so with targets declared, name them and
ask; with none, this is § 1's no-launch case.

**Physical-device completion.** The selected lane must build for the target's **actual platform**, so
inspect the dry run's lane, build destination, artifact substitution and ordered install/launch
after-steps first: **an iPhone target wired to a simulator build is an incomplete declaration**, and a
simulator `.app` cannot become a device artifact by being named in `after[]`. Repair the owning
declaration within authorized scope, or record its blocker through
[the discovery protocol](../../../docs/DISCOVERY.md). **Success requires the device-compatible build,
installation of that artifact and application launch to complete**, each reported: a dry run or
build-only result is **`launch incomplete`**, and missing install/launch steps are a declaration gap
even at exit `0`. **Reusable record discovery belongs to Nen's shared launch resolver**
([nen#204](https://github.com/zheref/nen/issues/204)), a temporary normalizer kept **linked** with its
owner and removal condition, and **unsupported extraction keys never added to an older binary.**

## 3. The core working directory, never a worktree

**A launch runs from the maintainer's own checkout and nowhere else** — not a `git worktree`, not a
subagent's copy, not a temporary clone. Built from a worktree it is a *different* build of a
*different* tree racing the one they are looking at, on the same port, derived-data directory and
bundle id; a fresh worktree also **fails the declaration's own preconditions**, and **launching writes
to a SHARED device**, so the isolation buys nothing on the axis that matters.

**nen will not stop you** — it renders the row with `cwd:` set to the worktree and no warning — so the
rule is this skill's, kept two ways: **resolve the core working directory explicitly** and pass it as
`--repo`, a path under `.claude/worktrees/` or any path `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` shows belongs
to another checkout **not** being it; and **a parallel subagent effort never launches**, reporting the
§ 4 dry-run argv verbatim and stopping.

**§ 3a · The one sanctioned exception — validating a declaration**, admissible from a non-core
checkout because [`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md) § 6 hands off a declaration PR nothing has ever run.
It holds only when **all four** are true: the maintainer's delegation **names the device and the
target**, in writing; the purpose is **a declaration under review**, never a turn's launch, `ren`'s
phase four or a composite; **no other session holds the app**; and **the report says so, in these
words** — *"validation launch from a non-core checkout: `<path>`; delegation names device `<name>` and
target `<key>`; declaration PR `<url>`"* — with the preconditions satisfied by hand. **Everything
outside those four is forbidden.**

## 4. Resolving the device, the dry run, and the command you paste

**The probe's three outcomes are LAUNCH-MIGRATION's**; what this skill does with each:

| Outcome | What amaterasu does |
|---|---|
| Present **and usable** | take its id and substitute `{device.id}` into the after-steps |
| **Present but NOT usable** | **Refuse, and do not fall back.** With `readyWhen` declared, **nen has already refused at exit `5`** naming the device, the state seen and the states accepted: relay it verbatim and name the on-device step that closes it ([`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md) § 3). With **no** rule, nen reports the row as resolved, so read the probe's state column here and **report the missing `readyWhen` as a declaration defect** |
| **Absent** | **Report it by name** — *"`<device.name>` is not connected; the probe saw: `<what it listed>`"* — then fall back to `launch.fallback`, saying so and which target it was |
| Absent, `launch.fallback` `null` | say so and stop; a device nobody plugged in is a fact, and picking a different one is a guess |
| No `device` declared | nothing to resolve — straight to the dry run |

**Never take the simulator fallback for a present-but-unusable device**: the fallback answers "nobody
plugged it in", and this device *is* plugged in, one tap from working.

```bash
nen shu <verb> --repo <core working directory> [--lane <lane>] --dry-run [--json]
nen shu <verb> --repo <core working directory> --target <name> [--lane <lane>]
```

- **`<verb>` is not a choice: it is `project.launch.<target>.verb`, exactly** — `dev` or `run`, a
  closed set — and nen does not carry a target across the two, the other being exit `2` naming the
  fix. With `--target` given, **the declared verb is checked before the lane's seat**, so an exit `4`
  there is a **real** seat and is quoted as one.
- The dry run prints the exact argv, the cwd, the env **names** and the declared artifacts, and spawns
  nothing. **The command pasted into the report and into chat is that `would run:` argv, verbatim** —
  copied, never re-typed, prettified, or turned back into the package script it came from.
- The bare run is **one line whether or not the target declares `args`**, nen appending them, and
  **an explicit `--lane` contradicting `project.launch.<name>.lane` is exit `2` naming both**.
- `dev` and `run` are **long-running**, so `--json` without `--dry-run` is refused at exit `2`, and
  **the launch is never backgrounded to get the terminal back** — say the app is running and what is
  holding the terminal.
- **Exit codes** are `claude/agents/kurapika.md` § *The `shu` verbs*'; here `1` means a declared step
  failed, so **identify from the output whether it was build, install or launch**, hand an
  authored-code failure to [`rasengan`](../rasengan/SKILL.md), and treat a failed install or launch as
  incomplete delivery; `3` is an excluded host, a **G5**, never retried; `4` is a real seat, quoted,
  after which the repository's documented command is run and said; `5` is the program not on `PATH`.
- **The after-steps are nen's to run**, as part of the same `--target` invocation, so nothing is run
  by hand. **Quote the dry run's `substitutes:` line into the report** rather than `artifacts:`: they
  answer different questions — what this build produces, and what the child receives.

## 5. Residue

**The core-working-directory check** is by hand, no verb knowing what a "core" checkout is, and
**§ 3a's four conditions are judged by hand too**. **Reading the device's state where no `readyWhen`
is declared** is residue **with a fix attached**, lapsing the moment a jujutsu PR writes the rule.
**There is no default target ever** and **no `--` passthrough**, an argv nobody declared being one
nobody reviewed; and **nothing in nen stops a long-running child**.

## 6. Authority and hard limits

- **Permitted:** run the lane's declared build/`dev` row from the core working directory, run a
  declared device probe, run the declared `after` steps, hand back the exact command.
- **Not permitted:** `nen shu deploy --run` in any form (a deploy stays behind **G3**, row
  `release-go`), and no push, commit, PR, label or release. **Not a gate event**; a disconnected
  device with no declared fallback is a stop-and-say, and an unsupported host (`3`) is its one **G5**.
- **Never launches from anything but the core working directory**, except under § 3a's four
  conditions, said in its own words; **never from a parallel effort**; and **never reaches § 3a from a
  composite** — an unattended path never launches from a non-core checkout.
- **Never falls back to a simulator for a present-but-unusable device**, to an undeclared device, or
  silently.
- **Never types a `shu` subcommand the target did not declare**, and never works around nen's exit `2`
  by dropping `--target`.
- **Never invents a target**, and **never asks when the declaration already answered** — the no-launch
  case is `no launch target declared; skipped` in the turn report, every turn, without a question.
- **Never substitutes a plausible command for a declared one**, re-types the pasted command from
  memory, or runs the bare lane verb for a target that declares `args`.
- **Never runs a deploy**, with or without `--run`, and **never claims the app is running** on a dry
  run or an exit code it did not read.
